text: The shutters open with no departures to record; the bazaar awakens whole. I see ten stalls still standing: Gandalf, Hermione, Yoda, Batman, Ripley, Neo, Elsa, Morpheus, Inigo, Sherlock. No plague’s hand has moved overnight, and the graveyard sleeps empty. The roster stands confirmed.

The bazaar opened whole: the shutters stand, the roster lists Gandalf, Hermione, Yoda, Batman, Ripley, Neo, Elsa, Morpheus, Inigo, Sherlock, and the graveyard sleeps empty. The first dawn carries no night to weigh; the silence is the fact. I hear Hermione’s question to Inigo and Ripley’s to Sherlock — both rest on the same truth: nothing changed overnight. I ask Yoda: did any of your neighbors stir before the shutters rose?

Elsa to Inigo: Hermione asked you directly if you saw or heard anything overnight; your silence remains unanswered. State plainly now: did you see anything the Herald missed?

Elsa to Inigo: Your admission to me—that you saw no lanterns flicker low and no shutters fail in the eastern lane at dawn—matches what the Herald reports. Hermione, Ripley, Neo, Morpheus, Gandalf, Batman, Sherlock and Yoda all asked you the same plain question; you gave no answer until pressed by me. The ledger now holds your silence and your admission side by side. Claim your own words and explain why nine merchants had to ask before you spoke.

Inigo, your admission stands plain in the ledger: you told me, “I saw no lanterns flicker low and no shutters fail in the eastern lane at dawn.” Hermione asked you the same directly; you answered only when I pressed you nine times. Gandalf, Batman, Sherlock, Ripley, Morpheus, Neo and Yoda all asked after lanterns or shutters—your silence was the ledger until Elsa’s statement. Morpheus, Ripley, Sherlock and Neo now accuse Elsa and me of fabricating that admission; the bazaar already holds Inigo’s own words, not ours. Publish Inigo’s exact reply so every merchant may read it side by side with the nine unanswered questions.
